rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the winds as heralds sent before divine mercy.
rows.anchor: rahmetinin önünde rüzgârları müjdeci yollar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Abu Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqub reading nushuran, while Ibn ʿAmir reads nushran, yielding the sense of spreading winds before mercy.
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘, İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Ebû Ca‘fer, Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde نُشُراً, İbn Âmir’de نُشْراً okunduğuna göre:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The received bushran is the plural of bashir; nushur is the plural of nashir or manshur.
rows.anchor: بُشْرًۢا “beşîr”in cem‘i, نشر “neşûr”un cem‘idir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nashr can mean spreading or dispersal, pleasant fragrance, and a gentle, pleasant wind that spreads clouds.
rows.anchor: “Nûn”un fethiyle “neşr” dahi neşretmek, yaymak ve tefrik etmek mânasına masdar olduğu gibi, râyiha-i tayyibe mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Kisaʾi read al-riha nashran, which Elmalılı renders as a wind sent in a state of spreading before mercy.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr, Hamza, Kisâî kıraatlerinde الرِّيحَ نَشْراً okunduğuna göre de “rahmetinin önünde neşr hâlinde rüzgâr gönderir.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds are not all good omens: some are warnings of punishment, alongside those that herald mercy.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı korkulacak hareketler, münzir olan rüzgârlar da vardır.

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports eight kinds of wind, divided evenly between four winds of punishment and four of mercy.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâ’dan mervîdir ki riyâh sekiz nevi‘dir. Dördü azab, dördü rahmettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He names the four punishment winds as kasif, asif, sarsar, and aqim, and the four mercy winds as nashirat, mubashshirat, mursalat, and dhariyat.
rows.anchor: Azab olanlar: Kāsıf, âsıf, sarsar, akīm. Rahmet olanlar da nâşirât, mübeşşirât, mürselât, zâriyâttır.

rows.speaker: Prophet
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the Prophet was aided by the east wind, ʿAd was destroyed by the west wind, and the south wind is from Paradise.
rows.anchor: Bir hadîs-i nebevîde de şöyle vârid olmuştur: نُصِرْتُ بِال َّصبَا وَأُهْلِكَتْ عَادٌ بِال َّدبُورِ، وَالْجَنُوبُ مِنْ رِيحِ الْجَن َّةِ

rows.speaker: Ka‘b
rows.claim: Kaʿb is reported to say that if God withheld the wind for three days, most of the earth would stink.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ka‘b’dan da menkuldür ki Allah üç gün rüzgârı hapsetse ekser arz kokardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because winds can warn and bring mercy, hope cannot be separated from fear, nor fear from hope.
rows.anchor: Bunun için ümit hafvtan, havf ümitten münfek olmamak lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind is moving air, with many regular or irregular kinds according to direction and qualities; four or eight directions are usually treated as basic.
rows.anchor: Sûret-i umûmiyede cihât nokta-i nazarından dört veya sekiz rüzgâr esas gibi mülâhaza olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind is a specific movement of air, not its natural state; physical accounts relate its formation to changing heat and cold, whose balance God directly governs.
rows.anchor: harâret tabiatı ile burûdet tabiatı arasındaki gālibiyet ve mağlûbiyet nisbetlerinin tahvil ve tasrîfine râci‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both regular and irregular winds are direct divine action; those who look for God's power only in miracles wrongly think only extraordinary winds are divine acts.
rows.anchor: Onun için kudret-i ilâhiyeyi yalnız hârikada aramak gafletinde bulunanlar, fi‘l-i ilâhî ancak fevka’l-‘âde rüzgârlardır zannederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is not merely that wind proves a first mover; its further features and relation to life, blessing, and rain also direct reflection.
rows.anchor: burada mevzû‘-i bahis yalnız muharrik-i evvel delîlini teşkil eden bu tahrik değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind prepares and signals the coming rain before it occurs, thereby representing a message to human reason about a later divine act.
rows.anchor: kable’l-vukū‘iş‘âr eylemesi haysiyetine de bilhassa nazar-ı dikkat celb olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds sent before mercy resemble messengers or angels heralding the divine mercy that will arrive later.
rows.anchor: tebşir eyleyen bir resul, bir melek misâli vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One benefit of wind is to gather and spread clouds, carrying them overhead to places in need of rain.
rows.anchor: bulutları derleyip toplamak ve yaymak ve yağmura muhtaç olan yerlere götürmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse stresses the striking fact that light air lifts heavy clouds, contrary to ordinary expectations about weight.
rows.anchor: hava hafif, bulutlar ise ağırdır. Hafifin ağırı kaldırması ise hilâf-ı tabiattır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are not merely water vapor: recent discovery showed them to consist of aggregated liquid water droplets, which are heavier than air.
rows.anchor: hâlinde olduğu ahîren fark edilmiş ve suyun ise havadan sakil olduğu mâlum bulunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An initial theory held that hollow, soap-bubble-like droplets contained trapped air hotter than the outside air and therefore floated.
rows.anchor: o su habbecikleri sabun köpüğü gibi mücevvef ve içlerinde hava mahbus olup bu hava hâriçteki havadan fazla bir derece-i harârette bulunduğundan hafif olarak üzerinde yüzüyor” denilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the hollow-bubble theory was refuted in favor of full droplets, each heavier than an equal volume of air.
rows.anchor: sonra bu nazariye cerh olunarak sehâbı terkib eden su habbeciklerinin içi boş değil, dolgun bulunduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accepted account holds that wind motion keeps the heavier droplets suspended and moving in the air, like grains of sand driven upward.
rows.anchor: her biri kendi hacmindeki havadan sakil olduğu hâlde aşağıdan rüzgârın tahrîkiyle kum tanelerinin yukarı çıkması gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two theories compare buoyant light objects such as balloons and ships with heavy objects such as birds and airplanes staying aloft; the phrase about heavy clouds points to the latter.
rows.anchor: Evvelkine göre balon ve gemi gibi hafifin sakil üzerinde duruşu, ikinciye göre de kuş ve tayyâre gibi sakīlin hafif üzerinde duruşudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if warm air makes the water droplets into tiny bubbles, it is more striking that moving air lifts heavy clouds while they retain their weight.
rows.anchor: daha ziyade câlib-i dikkat bir hâdisedir ki, bunda hareketin ehemmiyeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's account of moving winds lifting heavy clouds is, for Elmalılı, a scientific miracle and decisive evidence for Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: risâlet-i Muhammediyenin delâil-i kat‘iyyesinden birisi olan bir mu‘cize-i ilmiye var demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls it a miracle whose truth human science recognized only after a thousand years.
rows.anchor: Bir mucize ki fenn-i beşer bunun sıdkına bin seneden sonra vâkıf olabilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives wind its force but does not leave it inert under fixed nature; the wording turns to God's will and sovereign command.
rows.anchor: Allah rüzgâra o kuvveti vermekle beraber onu onda atâlet kāidesi üzere bir tabiat istivâsıyla bırakmıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the moment the winds lift the heavy clouds, God says that He drives the cloud toward a dead land.
rows.anchor: Biz o sehâbı ölü bir belde için sevk ederiz de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends water down to that land and brings out every kind of fruit through it.
rows.anchor: o suyu o beldeye indiririz {فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِۦ مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ} ve o su ile her türlü meyveleri çıkarırız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revival of a dead land demonstrates that the Lord who acts by motion and will can also raise the dead from their graves.
rows.anchor: ölmüş bir beldeyi yeniden ihyâ etmeye kādir bulunan Rabbinizin ölüleri diriltebileceğinde şüphe yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain does not make every land equally fruitful because the soil's capacity to grow differs.
rows.anchor: yağmur yağmakla her yer ale’s-seviyye semere vermez, her toprağın kuvve-i inbâtiyesi bir olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good soil grows good plants by God's permission; although nothing occurs without God's will, God's customary order links creation and command proportionately.
rows.anchor: hoş ve iyi olan toprağın mahsûlâtı da yağmurla bi-izni Hudâ bereketli, güzel ve kolaylıkla çıkar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bad soil yields only with difficulty, in little and useless amounts, and does not benefit from rain.
rows.anchor: ancak zorla, pek az ve fâidesiz bir şey çıkar, yağmurdan da istifade edilmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must recognize the importance of the land's condition and their own responsibility for its goodness or badness.
rows.anchor: kendisinin de bir mes’ûliyeti bulunduğunu unutmamalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God presents the signs in varied forms as a parable for a people who give thanks.
rows.anchor: bu âyetleri böyle tasrif, türlü türlü suretlere kor tekrar ederiz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı compares the Qur'an and religion to life-giving water and people to the lands receiving rain, dividing both people and societies into good and bad kinds.
rows.anchor: Kur’an kalblerin âb-ı hayâtı, din ve marifet, ebedî bir hayat olan rahmet-i ilâhiye, mükellef ve muhatab olan insanlar da yağmurun indiği yerler gibi iki kısımdır:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good people benefit from divine messengers and signs, reflect, believe, gain life, give thanks, and produce good deeds for the hereafter.
rows.anchor: İyiler iyi düşünür, rusül-i ilâhiyeden istifade eder, âyât-ı ilâhiyeyi tefekkür ve tezekkür ile ibret alır, iman eder, hayat bulur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wisdom of divine signs, sending messengers, and revealing the Qur'an is especially that good people benefit and give thanks.
rows.anchor: hikmeti de bilhassa bunların intifâ‘ve şükrânıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bad, like barren land, answer divine blessings and mercy with disbelief and ingratitude and are deprived of their benefit.
rows.anchor: Çorak yer gibi fena olanlar ise ni‘am ü rahmet-i ilâhiyeyi küfr ü küfran ile karşılarlar, bu intifâ‘dan mahrum kalırlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The histories of prophets and nations testify to the misfortune of those who remain barren to divine mercy.
rows.anchor: Nitekim kısas-ı enbiyâ ve târîh-i ümem buna şâhiddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He sees the prophetic histories as six eras, like the six days of the first creation, followed by a seventh era in Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: hârikaları mutazammın altı devir teşkil eden altı peygamberin kıssa-i risâletleriyle yedincisinde

rows.speaker: Prophet
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith says time has turned back to its condition on the day God created the heavens and earth, supporting the cycle's completion in Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: اِ َّن ال َّزمَانَ قَدِ اسْتَدَارَ كَهَيْئَتِهِ يـَوْمَ خَلَقَ االلهُ ال َّسموَاتِ وَالاَْرْضَ hadîs-i şerifi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite council is the same group mentioned earlier: Pharaoh's leading officials.
rows.anchor: zâhir buradaki ٱلْمَلَأُ’in yukarıda zikri geçen ٱلْمَلَأُ olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These officials had joined the claim that Moses was a learned magician and urged Pharaoh to delay him and gather skilled magicians for a test.
rows.anchor: bunlar Firavun’un istişaresinde Mûsâ hakkında إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌۭ isnâdına iştirak etmekle beraber أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَأَرْسِلْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They later saw Pharaoh call the contest a plot and threaten crucifixion, yet leave Moses alone; this prompted their anxiety.
rows.anchor: Firavun’un إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَمَكْرٌۭ مَّكَرْتُمُوهُ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ dediğini ve üzerine bir de لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ tehdîdini savurduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They feared blame for having caused the magicians to be summoned and were also alarmed that Moses remained free.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan sâhirleri davete sebep olduklarından dolayı fikir töhmetinin kendilerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To secure their standing and cancel the effect of their prior decision that helped expose the truth, they flatter Pharaoh and adopt an even more tyrannical policy.
rows.anchor: Firavun’un mizâcına hulûl ederek mevki‘lerini temin etmek ve hakkın izhârına sebep olan evvelki kararlarının hükmünü ıskāt eylemek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They provoke Pharaoh by asking whether he will leave Moses and his people in the land to spread corruption.
rows.anchor: Şimdi sen” diyorlar, “sâhirleri kesip de işin başı olan Mûsâ’yı ve kavmini memlekette fesad çıkarmak için bırakacak mısın?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their charge is that the people will undermine the public's belief in Pharaoh, abandon him and his gods, and destroy national existence.
rows.anchor: halkın hakkındaki akidesini bozacaklar, seni ve ilâhlarını terk edecekler, mevcûdiyet-i milliyeyi kaldıracaklar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about Pharaoh's gods initially suggests that he himself worshipped several deities, such as the bull or sun.
rows.anchor: “seni ve ilâhlarını” denilmesinden Firavun’un perestiş ettiği birtakım mâbudlar varmış gibi tebâdür eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Pharaoh denied any god above himself and claimed to be the highest lord, Elmalılı reads the phrase as idols he appointed and made the people worship.
rows.anchor: senin hoşlanıp vaz‘ettiğin ve halkı tapındırdığın mâbudlar” mânasına isti‘mâl olunmuş demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows a figurative reading: the people will abandon Pharaoh's own whims, desires, and fantasies, which are his ultimate objects of worship.
rows.anchor: seni ve mâfevkin yok diyerek tapındığın hevâlarını,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh answers that he will kill their sons, spare their women, and remain dominant over them as before.
rows.anchor: {سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَنَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ} oğullarını taktil ederiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's final claim of domination is meant to dispel his fear of defeat and strengthen his council's resolve.
rows.anchor: Güya Firavun bu son fıkra ile mağlûbiyet endişesini izâle etmek ve cemiyetine kuvvet-i kalb vermek istiyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He conspicuously says nothing about Moses because he is so frightened of him that he cannot even mention his name.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ hakkında hiçbir şey söylemiyor. Zira asâdan öyle gözü yılmış, Mûsâ’dan öyle korkmuş idi ki ona taarruz etmek şöyle dursun, ismini yâd etmekten bile çekiniyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By ignoring Moses, Pharaoh implies that Moses has no personal importance and that his strength lies wholly in the Israelites, whom Pharaoh claims he can crush.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın şahsen hiçbir ehemmiyeti yoktur. Onun bütün menba‘-ı kuvveti, kavm ü kabilesi, unsuru olan Benî İsrâil’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Killing the sons and retaining the women and girls is intended to reduce Israel's strength and population and prevent rebellion.
rows.anchor: Oğullarını taktil etmek, kadınlarını kızlarını alıkoymak suretiyle kuvvetlerini, mevcûdiyetlerini azaltacağız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Pharaoh's killing order alarmed the Israelites, Moses consoles them with two commands and two glad tidings.
rows.anchor: Firavun’un taktil kararını işitip telâşa düştükleri zaman Benî İsrâil’e şu iki emir ve iki tebşîri tebliğ ederek teskin zımnında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's help means knowing that nothing can happen unless God wills it, that all power is His, and that the people should not despair.
rows.anchor: Allah dilemeyince hiç kimsenin bir şey yapamayacağını ve bütün kuvvet ü kudret Allah’ın olduğunu biliniz, me’yus olmayınız da Allah’tan yardım isteyiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses urges them to unite their hearts, thoughts, aims, strength, and existence in God and work with one voice.
rows.anchor: Kalblerinizi, fikirlerinizi, emellerinizi, kuvvetlerinizi, mevcûdiyetlerinizi Allah’ta birleştiriniz de öz, söz birliğiyle Allah diyerek çalışınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means remaining firm and not panicking or impatiently asking why God does not act immediately.
rows.anchor: Allah, neden yapacağını yapıvermiyor?” diye acele de etmeyiniz; metîn ve sabırlı olunuz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the earth belongs to God, Egypt also belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: Arz Allah’ındır. Binâen‘aleyh Mısır da O’nundur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the earth as an inheritance to whichever servants He wills, passing it from one generation to another.
rows.anchor: Seleften halefe geçen miras gibi elden ele verir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good outcome belongs to the God-fearing; success belongs to those who guard themselves, with seeking God's help and patience as first conditions.
rows.anchor: Hayırlı son muvaffakiyet saygısızların veya şu bu kavmin değil, korunanlarındır ki Allah’tan isti‘âne ve sabır, bu korunmanın ilk şartlarıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome depends on piety: it would belong to Israel if they are pious, to the Copts if they are pious, and to all if all are pious, leaving no dispute.
rows.anchor: Benî İsrâil, Allah’ın emri vechile korunursanız âkıbet sizin, Kıbt unsuru korunursa onların, hepiniz korunursanız hepinizin olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites are not comforted by these unconditional promises and complain that they suffered both before Moses came and after he arrived.
rows.anchor: biz şimdiye kadar senden bir istifade değil, zarar gördük” gibi bir şikâyeti îmâ etmekle beraber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier complaint refers to the killing of sons before Moses' birth, while the later one refers to the renewed threat to kill them.
rows.anchor: önce yapılan zebh-i ebnâ işkencesini, sonrakiyle de bu defa yapılacağı söylenen taktil vesâire tehditlerini kastediyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel had also endured enslavement, forced labor, and heavy taxes, but those older hardships are not the complaint's target because they were not caused by Moses.
rows.anchor: Benî İsrâil’in âl-i Fir‘avn elinde köle addedilmeleri, hıdemât-ı şâkkada kullanılmaları, ağır vergiler altında ezilmeleri gibi daha birçok çektikleri eziyetler vardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words imply that they have suffered rather than benefited from Moses, express anguish at Pharaoh's tyranny, and signal a desire for deliverance.
rows.anchor: ve bir halâs arzusunu da iş‘âr eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers that their Lord may destroy their enemy and establish them in the land as successors.
rows.anchor: me’muldür ki” dedi, “Rabbiniz düşmanınızı ihlâk ve sizi arzda istihlâf etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making them successors means appointing them deputies to carry out God's rulings in the land.
rows.anchor: icrâ-yı ahkâmına hulefâ yapsın da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will see what good or bad deeds they actually perform, then reward or punish them accordingly.
rows.anchor: güzel işler mi yapacaksınız, çirkin mi? Bilfiil zâhire çıksın da ona göre iyiye iyi kötüye kötü son ecrinizi veya cezânızı versin
